## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- Only one independent source confirms the best tide.
- No survey, scientific or official source describes the shape of the bottom.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | High | Supported by 6 independent sources, including a published surf guide. |
| Swell size | Low | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 1 disagrees. |
| Swell period | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Wind | Low | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide; 3 disagree. |
| Tide | Moderate | Supported by one source (a surf magazine); 1 disagrees. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 2 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |
| Season | High | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a published surf guide. |
| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 6 independent sources, including a published surf guide. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Seven readable sources from seven publishers: Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, WSL, WannaSurf, Stormrider Surf Guides, Yeeew and Surf Atlas. No peer-reviewed or official source was found; Crossref returned nothing for J-Bay surf or Supertubes. WIND CONFLICT, still the main issue. The best or offshore winds given are: WSL best-conditions table SW/WSW (236), WannaSurf SW (225), Yeeew SW/S (202.5) and Surf-Forecast WSW (247.5). Only Surf-Forecast's WSW is within 45 deg of the profile's 290. Surf Atlas alone says the frequent winter NW winds are generally offshore (315), which agrees. Stormrider's J-Bay page (stormrider.surf/break/j-bay) says 'SW-W is offshore for most of the sections, while NW-NE Berg (or Devil) winds descend from the mountains, blowing into the barrels', with wind 'South Westerly'. That text is only in the page's script data, which the excerpt checker cannot see, so it was not recorded; it contradicts Surf Atlas's NW. Most readable evidence centres the offshore on about 225-250 deg, not 290. Swell direction: SSW/SW from WSL, Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas, WannaSurf and Stormrider (region). Yeeew's S/SE is the outlier and looks templated. Size: WSL 5-15 ft faces matches the profile. Wikipedia's 8-20 ft faces and Yeeew's 3-18 ft (my conversion) run higher; WannaSurf says best at 4-8 ft. Period: only WSL gives a number (12 s+), equal to the profile minimum. Tide: WSL (low to mid best, works all tides) and Yeeew (all) agree with 'all'; WannaSurf says mid. Seasonality: winter / May-August from Surf Atlas and Stormrider (region), and summer flat from Surf-Forecast. All agree with May-September. The Stormrider claims come from its St Francis Bay region page and are region-level.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3–5 ft | documented | S4 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 5–15 ft [S3] · 8–20 ft [S2] · 4–8 ft [S4] · waist high to triple overhead [S6] (face where stated) | conflicting | S2, S3, S4, S6 | no separate setting; working range 4–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 10 ft (3 m) or more (scale not stated) | documented | S4 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft (the page's own conversion; face or offshore height not stated); the other sizes in the evidence are best or optimal ranges, not minimums.
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 3m+ / 10ft+”
- **Ideal range**: WSL's best-conditions table gives 5-15 ft faces, Wikipedia gives an optimal 4-10 ft Hawaiian scale which it converts itself to about 8-20 ft faces, WannaSurf says it is best at 4-8 ft (scale not stated), and Yeeew says it gets good between waist high and triple overhead.
  - S3 (World Surf League): “Swell size: 5-15' faces”
  - S2 (Wikipedia): “Optimal size is considered to be from about 4 to 10 feet (Hawaiian scale), or about 8 to 20 feet wave faces.”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “The wave is best in the 4 – 8 ft category.”
  - S6 (Yeeew!): “It gets good between waist-high and triple overhead.”
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf says it holds up to 3 m+ / 10 ft+, an open-ended bound (scale not stated), so it holds at least 10 ft; no excerpt states an upper limit, and the best ranges of WSL and Wikipedia reach 15 and 20 ft faces.
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 3m+ / 10ft+”

- **Prime months**: Surf Atlas says the winter season between May and August brings the best swells and Stormrider says the frequent SW swells come in winter (region-wide, encoded June-August); the value is the months both share, May is the one-month difference, and Surf-Forecast says summer tends to be mostly flat.
  - S7 (Surf Atlas): “The winter season in the Southern Hemisphere (between May and August) brings the best swells to Jefferys Bay.”
  - S5 (Stormrider Surf Guides): “The frequent winter SW swells turn on dozens of classic pointbreaks”
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “although summer tends to be mostly flat”
- **Secondary season**: No excerpt states a secondary or shoulder season.
- **Swell sources**: Surf Atlas says the prime swells come as the bigger storms rage SSW around Cape St. Francis, WannaSurf that a strong storm from the southwest (or unusually the southeast) is needed, and Stormrider names frequent winter SW swells (region-wide).
  - S7 (Surf Atlas): “The absolute prime swells of all tend to come in the peak of winter as the bigger storms rage SSW around Cape St. Francis”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “A strong storm from the southwest, or the unusual southeast, is needed to push waves into the Bay.”
  - S5 (Stormrider Surf Guides): “The frequent winter SW swells turn on dozens of classic pointbreaks”
- **Wind patterns**: Surf Atlas says frequent NW winds are generally offshore and last basically all winter, and WannaSurf says the SW storms are almost always accompanied by offshore southwest winds; the two disagree on which wind is offshore.
  - S7 (Surf Atlas): “Those combine with frequent NW winds, which are generally offshore and last basically all winter.”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Such storms are almost always accompanied by offshore southwest winds.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · ideal range**: WSL's best-conditions table gives 5-15 ft faces, Wikipedia gives an optimal 4-10 ft Hawaiian scale which it converts itself to about 8-20 ft faces, WannaSurf says it is best at 4-8 ft (scale not stated), and Yeeew says it gets good between waist high and triple overhead.
- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: WSL (table SSW, Tomson SW), Surf-Forecast (SW), Surf Atlas (SSW storms), WannaSurf (a strong SW storm) and Stormrider (winter SW swells, region-wide) put the best swell at SSW to SW, while Yeeew says the best swells are S or SE, the more south the better.
- **Wind · offshore**: WSL's best-conditions table gives SW and WSW, WannaSurf says the storms bring offshore southwest winds, Yeeew gives SW or S as best and Surf-Forecast WSW as offshore, while Surf Atlas says the frequent winter NW winds are generally offshore; SW-S and NW are more than 45 deg apart.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: WannaSurf gives mid tide as the best position, while Yeeew says it works on all tides.
